entries.abstract: Improving control over physical qubits is a crucial component of quantum computing research. Here we report a superconducting fluxonium qubit with uncorrected coherence time T_{2}^{*}=1.48±0.13 ms, exceeding the state of the art for transmons by an order of magnitude. The average gate fidelity was benchmarked at 0.99991(1). Notably, even in the millisecond range, the coherence time is limited by material absorption and could be further improved with a more rigorous fabrication. Our demonstration may be useful for suppressing errors in the next generation quantum processors.

entries.abstract: Noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices pave the way for implementing quantum algorithms that offer quantum advantages over their classical counterparts. entries.title: Optimal Universal Bounds for Waves With Varied Coherence Based on Supremum and Infimum Coherence Spectra
entries.org: The University of Texas at Austin
entries.countryEvidence: institution country codes [US, US] → US
entries.abstract: ABSTRACT We establish a majorization‐based theory for bounding observables of waves with varied coherence. For any measurement, exact bounds are attained by the maximal and minimal elements in the set of input coherence spectra. The set's supremum and infimum—which may lie outside the set—provide optimal universal bounds: any alternative spectrum yielding universal bounds produces weaker constraints. We present an algorithm to compute the supremum and infimum and prove that they lie either at singular boundary points or strictly outside the set of coherence spectra.

entries.countryEvidence: no location match (auto-classified from Quantum Zeitgeist RSS, unverified)
entries.abstract: Until now, geometric control of quantum systems demanded either painstakingly slow operations or complex four-level designs. This work achieves arbitrary single-qubit gates in a genuinely nonadiabatic three-level system, directly addressing decay and dephasing, factors previously ignored or treated as afterthoughts. By embedding dissipation into the pulse design itself, a pathway towards more dependable quantum computation opens.

entries.countryEvidence: no location match (auto-classified from Quantum Zeitgeist RSS, unverified)
entries.abstract: Opposite spin orientations, revealed in paired Majorana corner states, now offer a direct route to verifying their quantum properties. Previously, confirming the spin structure of these states proved exceptionally difficult, hindering progress towards practical quantum computation. This work establishes a spin-resolved transport protocol, resilient to disorder, that links measurable conductance to the spin of these elusive quasiparticles.

entries.abstract: The way today's quantum computers report answers is fundamentally uncertain: each run yields a probability, and confirming a single result typically requires repeating the same calculation thousands of times. This makes quantum computing slow and costly to validate and limits its use in important applications such as drug discovery, secure communications, and large-scale optimization. This project addresses this challenge by pairing a quantum computation with a small electronic circuit that implements the same operation in a different physical form. entries.title: The Uncertainty Relation and the Determinacy Relation
entries.countryEvidence: institution country codes [UA] → UA
entries.abstract: The problem of measuring the energy of a quantum system, the process of emission of an electromagnetic field quantum, and their connection with the provisions of the Heisenberg uncertainty principle are considered. It is shown that the processes of measuring the energy of a quantum system and the time of transition between levels are performed not only simultaneously, but in a single act of measurement, and cannot be fulfilled in another way. This contradicts the physical ideas embedded in the uncertainty principle. As an alternative, the concept of "determinacy relations" is proposed.

entries.abstract: We investigate the asymptotic stability and ergodic properties of quantum trajectories under imperfect measurement, extending previous results established for the ideal case of perfect measurement. We establish a necessary and sufficient condition ensuring the convergence of the estimated trajectory, initialized from an estimated state, to the true trajectory. Building on this, we prove the uniqueness of the invariant measure and demonstrate convergence toward this measure.

entries.countryEvidence: NSF awardee country US
entries.abstract:
Experiments with ultracold quantum gases have changed the way we think about quantum dynamics and thermalization. The goal of these studies is to explore the beginning of thermalizing dynamics and to identify the mechanisms driving it in confined systems. One specific question that will be addressed is whether thermalization can occur under dynamics that is fully described by generalized hydrodynamics. The PI will also carry out outreach activities involving pedagogical talks and demo presentations at the local high school and a local elementary school.

entries.title: Extensions of Liouville quantum gravity
entries.countryEvidence: NSF awardee country US
entries.abstract: The project focuses on extensions of the theory of Liouville quantum gravity (LQG). LQG is a theory of random surfaces with connections to many areas of math and physics. In physics, LQG surfaces can be viewed as a model of quantum gravity in a two-dimensional universe, and hence as a toy model for quantum gravity in the real world. LQG surfaces are also important in string theory and conformal field theory. There is extensive mathematical literature on LQG, including deep connections to other mathematical objects such as random curves, random graphs, random permutations, Riemann surfaces,…

entries.countryEvidence: NSF awardee country US
entries.abstract: This interdisciplinary project, titled 'CAREER: Advancing protein-based qubits into the single-molecule regime,' explores fluorescent proteins as an innovative platform for quantum sensing. Recently, the PI's laboratory successfully encoded a qubit into the metastable spin state of an enhanced yellow fluorescent protein (eYFP), demonstrating coherence times of approximately 16 µs. With a size of only 3 nm and complete biocompatibility, these protein-based qubits offer significant advantages over conventional quantum sensing technologies, such as nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond.…

entries.countryEvidence: no location match (auto-classified from Quantum Zeitgeist RSS, unverified)
entries.abstract: Researchers at Laboratoire de Physique de l’École Normale Supérieure, ENS, investigated a complementarity relation between predictability and quantum coherence, representing particle-like and wave-like behavior in wave–particle duality, in a multi-path setup. entries.title: Asymptotically optimal joint phase and dephasing-strength estimation using spin-squeezed states
entries.countryEvidence: institution country codes [PL, PL] → PL
entries.abstract: We show an explicit $N$-qubit protocol involving one-axis-twisted spin squeezed states, that allows for simultaneous phase and dephasing strength estimation with precision that asymptotically matches fundamental quantum metrological bounds. The relevance of the protocol goes beyond this particular model, since any uncorrelated noise quantum metrological model, that allows for at most constant asymptotic quantum enhancement, can be reduced to this problem via an appropriately tailored quantum error-correction procedure.

entries.title: Researchers Map Hidden Edge States in Dissipative Superconductor
entries.countryEvidence: no location match (auto-classified from Quantum Zeitgeist RSS, unverified)
entries.abstract: Normally, a material’s decay rate reveals its underlying quantum structure, but in a novel topological superconductor, this connection fails. The Majorana rapidity matrix splits into independent sectors at zero chemical potential, yet local measurements detect only a combined decay rate, remaining oblivious to hidden topological states. This sector-blindness contrasts with other dissipative systems and unveils a more nuanced picture of non-Hermitian topology.

entries.title: Attention-Like Hebbian Learning from Quantum Probability Flow and Quantum-Annealer Tests
entries.countryEvidence: institution country codes [JP, JP] → JP
entries.abstract: We propose a quantum probability-flow principle for deriving local learning rules in associative memory. A transverse field defines leakage channels from data states, and minimizing the measured survival loss gives stability-driven updates. For imaginary-time, dephased dynamics, the local leakage-free energy is the log-sum-exp of energy gaps; its gradient is a softmax-weighted Hebbian rule. Real-time stability instead yields a power-law weighting. D-Wave standard- and fast-anneal tests of a one-hot attention forward map are better fitted by an effective softmax than by a Lorentzian power law.

entries.abstract: Increasing the gravitational coupling between particles preferentially enhances collective coherence, a finding that refines understanding of quantum resilience in massive systems. entries.abstract: ABSTRACT We have constructed and run a Bell test of local realism focusing on the objectivity criterion. Objectivity means that the outcomes are macroscopically confirmed by a few observers at each party. The IBM Quantum and IonQ devices turn out to be sufficiently accurate to pass such an extended Bell‐type test, although at the price of communication loopholes and residual but statistically significant signaling. The test also serves as a benchmark of entanglement spread across larger sets of qubits.

entries.title: The Quantum Coherence as a Phase Property of the Wave Function
entries.countryEvidence: institution country codes [BG] → BG
entries.abstract: The quantum coherence as a phase property of the most fundamental quantum mechanical entity, the wave function, is explained for the first time. Phase-sensitive nonadiabatic dressed states, arising from the interaction of a quantum system and a coherent external electromagnetic field, are used in these considerations. Two types of phase correlations in the multilevel phase-sensitive nonadiabatic dressed states are found: a rapidly changing phase correlation between the real and the virtual components and a stationary phase correlation between different virtual components of these states.

notes.author: E. Johnston
notes.headline: Error-correction and networking dominate the current preprint flow
notes.body: The newest quant-ph papers cluster around fault-tolerant codes and entanglement distribution rather than raw qubit records. That shift, from building bigger chips to making existing ones reliable, is the tell that the field is moving from demonstration toward engineering. Watch whether the US share of these papers holds as Chinese groups publish more on the same problems.

notes.author: E. Johnston
notes.headline: Below-threshold error correction is the milestone that actually matters
notes.body: Google's Willow result and IBM's stated path to 100k physical qubits are the two anchors here. The qubit-count headlines matter less than whether error rates fall as systems grow, which is the thing that decides if any of this scales. This stage has no live feed by design, so treat the five entries as a curated watchlist, not a census.

notes.author: E. Johnston
notes.headline: Procurement is still government and cloud, not end users
notes.body: DARPA's benchmarking program and EuroHPC's co-located systems show that the buyers are states and supercomputing centers, not commercial customers solving real problems. That is the honest state of adoption in 2026. The policy question is whether public procurement sustains the vendors long enough for a commercial market to appear.

notes.author: E. Johnston
notes.headline: US funding is visible, Chinese funding is not
notes.body: NSF awards give a clean read on US public spending on quantum, but there is no comparable public feed for China's NSFC or the provincial programs that carry much of the weight. Treat this stage as a floor on Western investment rather than a balanced comparison. The gap is a data-access problem, not evidence that Beijing is spending less.
